basis: Concise summary of standard anatomical references (e.g. Gray's Anatomy; Moore's Clinically Oriented Anatomy) and the Mathes–Nahai muscle classification. Page references are NOT verified. Every entry is verificationStatus=needs_review.

muscles.name: Latissimus dorsi
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of T7–T12 and the thoracolumbar fascia, posterior iliac crest, lower 3–4 ribs; small slip from the inferior angle of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular groove of the humerus
muscles.action: Adducts, extends and medially rotates the arm

minor: Segmental perforators of posterior intercostal and lumbar arteries

muscles.pearl: Thoracodorsal pedicle runs on the deep surface; the serratus branch arises from it distally

muscles.name: Pectoralis major
muscles.origin: Clavicular head: medial half of clavicle. Sternocostal head: sternum and upper 6 costal cartilages. Abdominal part: aponeurosis of external oblique
muscles.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular groove of the humerus
muscles.action: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; clavicular part flexes the arm

dominant: Pectoral branch of the thoracoacromial artery

relatedFlaps: Internal mammary artery perforator (IMAP) flap region
muscles.pearl: Thoracoacromial pedicle lies on the deep surface, found on the undersurface of pectoralis major along a line from acromion to xiphoid (surface marking)

muscles.name: Pectoralis minor
muscles.origin: Ribs 3–5 near the costal cartilages
muscles.insertion: Coracoid process of the scapula
muscles.action: Protracts and depresses the scapula; stabilises it against the chest wall

dominant: Pectoral branch of the thoracoacromial artery

relatedFlaps: Rarely used as a flap (e.g. facial reanimation)
muscles.pearl: Lies deep to pectoralis major; the thoracoacromial and lateral thoracic vessels pass around its borders

muscles.name: Serratus anterior
muscles.origin: External surfaces of the upper 8–9 ribs
muscles.insertion: Costal surface of the medial border of the scapula
muscles.action: Protracts the scapula and rotates it upward; holds the scapula against the chest wall

dominant: Serratus branch of the thoracodorsal artery (lower slips)

muscles.pearl: Preserve the long thoracic nerve and the upper slips to avoid scapular winging

muscles.name: Trapezius
muscles.origin: External occipital protuberance, medial third of superior nuchal line, ligamentum nuchae, spinous processes of C7–T12
muscles.insertion: Lateral third of clavicle, acromion and spine of scapula
muscles.action: Elevates, retracts and rotates the scapula

dominant: Transverse cervical artery (superficial/dorsal branches); dorsal scapular artery in some patterns

muscles.nerveSupply: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) motor, with C3–C4 proprioceptive fibres
muscles.pearl: Four or five angiosome territories depending on the origin of the dorsal scapular artery (Neligan Ch. 23); harvest risks shoulder dysfunction if CN XI is injured

muscles.name: Deltoid
muscles.origin: Lateral third of the clavicle, acromion, spine of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus
muscles.action: Abducts the arm; clavicular part flexes, spinal part extends

dominant: Deltoid branch of the thoracoacromial artery

relatedFlaps: Deltoid / posterior circumflex humeral perforator fasciocutaneous flap
muscles.pearl: Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral vessels pass through the quadrangular space

muscles.name: Rectus abdominis
muscles.origin: Pubic crest and pubic symphysis
muscles.insertion: Xiphoid process and 5th–7th costal cartilages
muscles.action: Flexes the trunk; compresses the abdomen

dominant: Deep superior epigastric artery (from the internal thoracic)

muscles.nerveSupply: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11) and subcostal nerve (T12), segmental
muscles.pearl: The two epigastric systems anastomose within the muscle (reciprocal size, law of equilibrium); preserve segmental nerves in muscle-sparing harvest to limit hernia and weakness

muscles.name: External oblique
muscles.origin: External surfaces of the lower 8 ribs
muscles.insertion: Linea alba, pubic tubercle and anterior iliac crest
muscles.action: Flexes and rotates the trunk; compresses the abdomen

dominant: Segmental branches of lower intercostal, subcostal and lumbar arteries

muscles.nerveSupply: Lower intercostal nerves (T7–T11) and subcostal nerve (T12)
relatedFlaps: Rarely used as a muscle flap; its fascia is a closure layer in abdominal flap donor sites
muscles.pearl: Lies lateral to the rectus sheath — relevant when closing DIEP/TRAM donor sites

muscles.name: Internal oblique
muscles.origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, anterior two-thirds of the iliac crest, lateral two-thirds of the inguinal ligament
muscles.insertion: Lower borders of the last 3–4 ribs, linea alba, pubic crest via the conjoint tendon
muscles.action: Flexes and rotates the trunk; compresses the abdomen

dominant: Ascending branch of the deep circumflex iliac artery
minor: Segmental branches of lower intercostal, subcostal and lumbar arteries (verify)

muscles.nerveSupply: Lower thoracic nerves (T7–T12) and L1 (iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal)
relatedFlaps: Deep circumflex iliac artery (DCIA) osteomuscular / osteocutaneous flap
muscles.pearl: Type IV neurovascular classification (Neligan Table 23.1: fused-somite muscle)

muscles.name: Gluteus maximus
muscles.origin: Posterior gluteal line of the ilium, posterior sacrum and coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament, thoracolumbar fascia
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial tract (superficial three-quarters) and gluteal tuberosity (deep quarter)
muscles.action: Extends and laterally rotates the hip
muscles.pearl: Piriformis is the landmark: the superior gluteal vessels exit above it, the inferior gluteal vessels below it

muscles.name: Gluteus medius
muscles.origin: External surface of the ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the greater trochanter
muscles.action: Abducts the hip; stabilises the pelvis
relatedFlaps: Lies deep to the SGAP perforator path
muscles.pearl: The superior gluteal vessels and nerve run between gluteus medius and minimus

muscles.name: Tensor fasciae latae
muscles.origin: Anterior iliac crest and anterior superior iliac spine
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial tract
muscles.action: Tenses the fascia lata; assists hip flexion, abduction and medial rotation

dominant: Ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery

muscles.pearl: The pedicle enters the deep surface in the proximal third (surface landmark: ASIS)

muscles.name: Rectus femoris
muscles.origin: Straight head: anterior inferior iliac spine. Reflected head: superior acetabular rim
muscles.insertion: Base of the patella via the quadriceps tendon, then tibial tuberosity
muscles.action: Extends the knee; flexes the hip

dominant: Descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery

relatedFlaps: Rectus femoris myocutaneous (abdominal wall, groin, perineum)
Medial boundary of the plane for the ALT flap
muscles.pearl: The ALT septum lies between rectus femoris and vastus lateralis

muscles.name: Vastus lateralis
muscles.origin: Greater trochanter, intertrochanteric line, lateral lip of the linea aspera, lateral intermuscular septum
muscles.insertion: Lateral border of the patella and quadriceps tendon
muscles.action: Extends the knee

dominant: Descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery (lateral branch)

relatedFlaps: ALT flap (musculocutaneous perforators pass through it)
muscles.pearl: The motor nerve to vastus lateralis runs with the descending branch — preserve it during pedicle dissection

muscles.name: Sartorius
muscles.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine
muscles.insertion: Proximal medial tibia (pes anserinus)
muscles.action: Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip; flexes the knee

dominant: Segmental branches of the superficial femoral artery
minor: Ascending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery proximally (verify)

muscles.pearl: Forms the roof of the femoral (adductor) canal; the femoral vessels lie deep to it

muscles.name: Gracilis
muscles.origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the proximal tibia (pes anserinus)
muscles.action: Adducts the thigh; flexes the knee

dominant: Branch of the medial circumflex femoral artery (main pedicle, enters proximally)
minor: Distal branches from the superficial femoral artery

muscles.nerveSupply: Anterior branch of the obturator nerve (L2–L4)
muscles.pearl: The cutaneous supply over gracilis is tenuous because the muscle is mobile beneath the deep fascia (Neligan Ch. 23)

muscles.name: Biceps femoris
muscles.origin: Long head: ischial tuberosity. Short head: lateral lip of the linea aspera
muscles.insertion: Head of the fibula (and lateral tibial condyle)
muscles.action: Flexes the knee; long head extends the hip

dominant: Perforating branches of the profunda femoris artery

muscles.nerveSupply: Long head: tibial division of the sciatic nerve. Short head: common fibular division
relatedFlaps: Biceps femoris V-Y advancement (ischial pressure sore)
muscles.pearl: The sciatic nerve and the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve lie deep to the long head

muscles.name: Semitendinosus
muscles.origin: Ischial tuberosity (common tendon with the long head of biceps femoris)
muscles.insertion: Proximal medial tibia (pes anserinus)
muscles.action: Flexes the knee; extends the hip; medially rotates the leg

dominant: Branches of the inferior gluteal and medial circumflex femoral arteries (proximal)
Perforating branches of the profunda femoris (distal)

muscles.nerveSupply: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.origin: Medial head: posterior femur above the medial condyle. Lateral head: lateral femoral condyle
muscles.insertion: Calcaneus via the Achilles tendon
muscles.action: Plantarflexes the ankle; flexes the knee
muscles.nerveSupply: Tibial nerve branches, one per head (S1–S2)
relatedFlaps: Medial / lateral gastrocnemius flap (knee and proximal tibia)
muscles.pearl: The sural nerve and small saphenous vein lie in the groove between the two heads; each head is an independent neurovascular unit

muscles.name: Soleus
muscles.origin: Posterior fibular head and proximal fibula, soleal line and medial border of the tibia
muscles.insertion: Calcaneus via the Achilles tendon
muscles.action: Plantarflexes the ankle

dominant: Branches of the popliteal and posterior tibial arteries (proximal)
minor: Segmental posterior tibial and peroneal perforators (distal)

relatedFlaps: Soleus (hemi- or whole) flap for middle-third tibial defects
muscles.pearl: Three angiosome territories (Neligan Table 23.2); many short vessels anastomose freely within the muscle

muscles.name: Tibialis anterior
muscles.origin: Lateral tibial condyle, upper two-thirds of the lateral tibia, interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal
muscles.action: Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot

dominant: Segmental branches of the anterior tibial artery

relatedFlaps: Neighbour of the anterior tibial perforators
muscles.pearl: One territory (anterior tibial); the anterior compartment is the one most vulnerable to ischaemia

muscles.name: Fibularis (peroneus) longus
muscles.origin: Head and upper two-thirds of the lateral fibula
muscles.insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal (plantar)
muscles.action: Everts the foot; plantarflexes the ankle
muscles.pearl: Peroneal septocutaneous perforators run in the posterior intermuscular septum between the peroneal muscles and soleus

muscles.name: Fibularis (peroneus) brevis
muscles.origin: Distal two-thirds of the lateral fibula
muscles.insertion: Tuberosity at the base of the fifth metatarsal
muscles.action: Everts the foot
relatedFlaps: Distally based peroneus brevis muscle flap (lateral malleolus / foot)

muscles.name: Flexor hallucis longus
muscles.origin: Posterior distal two-thirds of the fibula and interosseous membrane
muscles.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the great toe
muscles.action: Flexes the great toe; plantarflexes the ankle
relatedFlaps: Cuff of FHL is taken with the fibula free flap
muscles.pearl: The peroneal vessels run in or against FHL; over-harvest can cause great-toe flexion contracture

muscles.name: Brachioradialis
muscles.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
muscles.insertion: Distal radius, base of the styloid process
muscles.action: Flexes the elbow (mid-pronated position)
muscles.pearl: The radial artery lies between brachioradialis and flexor carpi radialis; the superficial radial nerve runs under brachioradialis

muscles.name: Palmaris longus
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor origin)
muscles.insertion: Flexor retinaculum and palmar aponeurosis
muscles.action: Weak wrist flexor; tenses the palmar aponeurosis
relatedFlaps: Tendon graft donor; vascularised tendon in radial forearm flap
muscles.pearl: Absent in a minority of people

muscles.name: Flexor carpi radialis
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle (common flexor origin)
muscles.insertion: Bases of the second and third metacarpals
muscles.action: Flexes and abducts the wrist
relatedFlaps: Landmark for the radial forearm flap pedicle
muscles.pearl: The radial artery lies lateral to the FCR tendon at the distal forearm

muscles.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
muscles.origin: Humeral head: medial epicondyle. Ulnar head: olecranon and posterior border of the ulna
muscles.insertion: Pisiform, hamate and fifth metacarpal
muscles.action: Flexes and adducts the wrist
muscles.pearl: With flexor digitorum profundus it is supplied only by the ulnar artery or recurrent interosseous branches (Neligan Ch. 23)

muscles.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.origin: Sternal head: manubrium. Clavicular head: medial third of the clavicle
muscles.insertion: Mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line
muscles.action: Rotates the head to the opposite side; flexes the neck

minor: Inferior thyroid and transverse cervical arteries (inferior)

muscles.nerveSupply: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) with C2–C3
muscles.pearl: Four territories; a skin paddle at the lower pole has a high incidence of loss because of its poor blood supply (Neligan Ch. 23)

muscles.name: Platysma
muscles.origin: Fascia over the upper pectoralis major and deltoid
muscles.insertion: Inferior border of the mandible, lower-face skin and SMAS
muscles.action: Depresses the lower lip and mandible; tenses neck skin

dominant: Submental branch of the facial artery (superior)
minor: Transverse cervical and inferior thyroid arteries (inferior)

muscles.nerveSupply: Cervical branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscles.pearl: Can be raised on a superior or inferior pedicle; protect the marginal mandibular nerve

muscles.name: Temporalis
muscles.origin: Temporal fossa and temporal fascia
muscles.insertion: Coronoid process and anterior ramus of the mandible
muscles.action: Elevates and retracts the mandible

dominant: Deep temporal arteries (from the maxillary artery)
minor: Middle temporal artery (from the superficial temporal)

muscles.pearl: Two territories (Neligan Table 23.3); can be raised on either vascular pedicle

muscles.name: Masseter
muscles.origin: Zygomatic arch
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the mandibular ramus and angle
muscles.action: Elevates the mandible

dominant: Masseteric branch of the maxillary artery

relatedFlaps: Masseter muscle flap (facial reanimation, intraoral defects)
muscles.pearl: Two territories (Neligan Table 23.3); the parotid duct and buccal/marginal mandibular branches lie close

muscles.name: Teres major
muscles.origin: Dorsal surface of the inferior angle and lower lateral border of the scapula
muscles.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular groove
muscles.action: Adducts and medially rotates the arm

dominant: Branches of the circumflex scapular and thoracodorsal arteries (verify)

relatedFlaps: Scapular / parascapular flap (boundary of the triangular space)
muscles.pearl: The circumflex scapular artery passes through the triangular space (teres major, teres minor, long head of triceps)

muscles.name: Triceps brachii
muscles.origin: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle. Lateral head: posterior humerus above the radial groove. Medial head: posterior humerus below the groove
muscles.insertion: Olecranon
muscles.action: Extends the elbow

minor: Superior ulnar collateral and posterior circumflex humeral branches

relatedFlaps: Lateral arm flap (septum between triceps and brachialis/brachioradialis)
muscles.pearl: Lateral arm flap perforators come from the descending branches of the profunda brachii along the lateral intermuscular septum

muscles.name: Abductor hallucis
muscles.origin: Medial calcaneal tuberosity and flexor retinaculum
muscles.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe
muscles.action: Abducts and flexes the great toe
